title: Part 1
text: Around thirty fish lie packed into one small patch of Bolivian rock. Something killed them fast.

title: Part 2
text: Those fish are Sacabambaspis, a jawless fish about twenty-five centimeters long that lived in Ordovician seas roughly 450 million years ago.
nxt: Their fossils come from the Anzaldo Formation near Cochabamba. Most fossil fish are found alone, as scattered plates.

title: Part 4
text: Think about what that means. Sea animals live in salt water. If a flood of fresh water pours into a shallow bay, the water around them changes fast.
nxt: At the same time, mud can bury animals alive. Sudden burial is the key. It protected the bodies from scavengers and decay, and that is how a fragile fish became a fossil.

title: Part 5
text: Some writers suggest a big storm was the trigger. That part is likely, but it is still an interpretation, not a proven fact. We cannot go back and watch.

title: Part 6
text: Here is where I need to be careful. You may read that all the fish point in the same direction because of ocean currents. I could not find a source for that, so I am not going to tell you it is true.
nxt: What we can say is that the rocks show a rapid burial of animals that lived near the shore.
